subject: Clarify console-friendly DPA + subprocessor snippets for procurement
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, legal@acme.com
Date: 2028-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Clarify DPA snippets for hosted API console

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for taking this on. Our procurement team has a short checklist for vendors for this week’s procurement review. They asked for two short, public-facing blurbs we can include in our SOW/attestation packet and in the console: (1) a 1–2 sentence plain-language description of what a "subprocessor" is and when Redwood shares data with them; and (2) a 1–2 sentence explanation of international data movement and safeguards (e.g., SCCs, adequacy).

Can you provide candidate copy we can paste into our procurement form and a slightly longer paragraph we can put in the console “Data & Privacy” modal? It would be helpful if the console variant is written for non-legal users (customer success / IT) and includes a short note about retention windows.

Attached: Acme_Security_Checklist.pdf (we flagged the sections where your copy will appear).

Timeline: procurement meeting on Friday (2028-04-22). Would 48 hours work?

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Legal / Acme Corp

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify DPA snippets for hosted API console

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. We can get you a set of three pieces:

- A single-line marketing-friendly blurb for procurement (1 sentence).
- A short, plain-language console blurb (2–3 sentences) for the Data & Privacy modal.
- A DPA-friendly paragraph (3–5 sentences) that can be referenced in contracts and procurement packets.

A couple quick questions that will affect wording: do you require explicit mention of which legal transfer mechanism (SCCs vs adequacy) should be highlighted? Also, do you want us to call out log retention windows by default (we typically keep request logs for troubleshooting for up to 30 days by default unless a customer requests a different setting under a contract)?

If that default is acceptable to call out, we’ll include a one-line retention statement. We’ll aim to send the first draft within 36 hours. I’ve attached a first-pass markdown file (redwood-console-dpa-snippets-v1.md) so you can comment inline.

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify DPA snippets for hosted API console

Evelyn —

I reviewed the v1 draft and left inline suggestions in the attached file, but here are the main edits I think will help procurement and non-legal buyers:

1) Replace the term "subprocessor" with "third-party service" in the console blurb and add a hover tooltip that says: "Third-party services help us operate or secure the product (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring, storage)."

2) For the DPA paragraph, we should be explicit that we require subprocessors to meet the same contractual privacy and security obligations as Redwood. Suggested sentence: "When we use third-party services to operate or improve the Hosted API, we contractually require them to protect customer data to the same standard as Redwood."

3) Keep the retention language short and concrete. Proposed: "Request logs are retained for troubleshooting for up to 30 days by default; customers can request a different retention policy under their contract."

I’m attaching redwood-console-dpa-snippets-v2.md with edits.

- Laura
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify DPA snippets for hosted API console

All —

Couple small copy nits and a console UX suggestion: when we reference international transfer safeguards, call out that we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where required and on adequacy decisions where applicable. Proposed console sentence: "When data moves outside your region, we protect it with recognized safeguards like EU Standard Contractual Clauses or rely on countries with an adequacy decision."

UX note: add the console path where customers can request data residency or retention changes: Console > Settings > Data & Privacy. I added that link to the v2 md.

Kimberly
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify DPA snippets for hosted API console

Quick note on tone for the one-liner the procurement team will see — they like an explicit signal about training: "We do not use customer prompt data to train our base models without an explicit opt-in." If legal is good with that, I can make a version that’s marketing-friendly and one that’s contract-safe.

Also: confirming the 30-day default retention callout is accurate for Hosted API request logs. We should surface the opt-in/opt-out for longer retention in the console modal.

— Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, legal@acme.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Plain-language DPA + console snippets (attached)

Hi Sarah and team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are two files: (1) redwood-console-dpa-snippets-v2.md — console-friendly copy and UX notes; and (2) redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf — a one-page summary procurement can include in the packet. Below are the three text snippets we discussed (copy is cleared by legal & privacy as of 2028-04-22):

1) Procurement one-liner (1 sentence):
"Redwood Inference uses third-party services only to operate and secure the Hosted API; we contractually require those vendors to protect customer data to the same standard as Redwood."

2) Console modal blurb (2–3 sentences, plain language):
"We sometimes use trusted third-party services (for example, cloud providers and monitoring tools) to run the Hosted API. We require those services to follow the same privacy and security rules we do. When data moves across borders, we protect it with recognized safeguards such as EU Standard Contractual Clauses or by relying on adequacy decisions."

Console UX note: add a tooltip on "third-party services" that says "Services we use to run or secure the product; names and locations are listed in our subprocessor map." Path: Console > Settings > Data & Privacy.

3) DPA paragraph (contract-friendly):
"Redwood may engage subprocessors (third-party service providers) to perform processing necessary to provide the Hosted API. We require subprocessors to comply with contractual obligations at least as protective as those set out in this DPA, and we maintain a publicly available subprocessor map. Where personal data is transferred across international borders, Redwood relies on appropriate safeguards (for example, EU Standard Contractual Clauses) or on an adequacy decision where available. Request logs are retained for troubleshooting for up to 30 days by default; customers may request tailored retention terms through their contract or via Console > Settings > Data & Privacy."

Next steps: let me know if Acme needs the redlineable DPA amendment (we can surface a DocuSign/track-changes package), or if the procurement team prefers just the one-pager and console copy. I’ve also shared the working folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-dpa-snippets and created HubSpot note HS-4321.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-console-dpa-snippets-v2.md, redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf
